# Slice iterators

The iterators an array, vector or deque hands out to walk its elements by copy or by pointer.

<h2 id="value-iterator"><code>ValueIterator&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct ValueIterator<T> {
    // private fields
}
```

An iterator that yields each element of a run by copy.
The element type must be copyable: a move-only element yielded by value would leave the container holding
something it no longer owns. Use [`ReferenceIterator`](/docs/api/collections/iterators#reference-iterator) for those.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L23)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Constructors**

<h3 id="value-iterator-new"><code>ValueIterator</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ValueIterator(items: T[..]) -> ValueIterator<T>
```

An iterator over `items`, positioned before the first element.
`items` is borrowed and must outlive the iterator.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
The storage must not be grown, freed or otherwise moved while this is alive.

| Name    | Type    | Description          |
| ------- | ------- | -------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the elements to take |

**Returns**: a cursor yielding copies of those elements

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L40)

**Implements Iterator**

`ValueIterator<T>` conforms to `Iterator`.

<h3 id="value-iterator-next"><code>Next</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Next(self: &var ValueIterator<T>) -> T?
```

The next element, or `none` once the run is exhausted.
`self` is borrowed mutably and advanced. An exhausted iterator keeps reporting `none`.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the next element, or `none` at the end

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L51)

<h2 id="reference-iterator"><code>ReferenceIterator&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct ReferenceIterator<T> {
    // private fields
}
```

An iterator that yields a pointer to each element of a run.
Works for any element type, including one that owns something and may not be copied: the pointer borrows the
element where it sits rather than taking it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L64)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Constructors**

<h3 id="reference-iterator-new"><code>ReferenceIterator</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ReferenceIterator(items: T[..]) -> ReferenceIterator<T>
```

An iterator over `items`, positioned before the first element.
`items` is borrowed and must outlive the iterator.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
Every pointer this yields points into the storage, so the storage must not be grown, freed or moved while
this or any pointer it yielded is still in use.

| Name    | Type    | Description          |
| ------- | ------- | -------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the elements to take |

**Returns**: a cursor yielding those elements' addresses

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L82)

**Implements Iterator**

`ReferenceIterator<T>` conforms to `Iterator`.

<h3 id="reference-iterator-next"><code>Next</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Next(self: &var ReferenceIterator<T>) -> (*T)?
```

A pointer to the next element, or `none` once the run is exhausted.
`self` is borrowed mutably and advanced. The pointer borrows the element and takes ownership of nothing.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the next element, or `none` at the end

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L93)

<h2 id="mutable-reference-iterator"><code>MutableReferenceIterator&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct MutableReferenceIterator<T> {
    // private fields
}
```

An iterator that yields a writable pointer to each element of a run.
Elements remain in their storage, so move-only elements can be modified without copying or moving them.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L105)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Constructors**

<h3 id="mutable-reference-iterator-new"><code>MutableReferenceIterator</code></h3>

```rux
pub func MutableReferenceIterator(items: var T[..]) -> MutableReferenceIterator<T>
```

An iterator over `items`, positioned before the first element.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
The storage must outlive the iterator and every pointer it yields. Do not grow, shrink, free, or move the
storage while any of them is in use. Coordinate access through aliases to the same elements.

| Name    | Type        | Description                        |
| ------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `items` | `var T[..]` | the elements to borrow for writing |

**Returns**: a cursor yielding writable addresses

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L122)

**Implements Iterator**

`MutableReferenceIterator<T>` conforms to `Iterator`.

<h3 id="mutable-reference-iterator-next"><code>Next</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Next(self: &var MutableReferenceIterator<T>) -> (*var T)?
```

The next writable element pointer, or `none` once exhausted.
Advances the cursor without copying, moving, or destroying an element. An exhausted cursor stays exhausted.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the next element's address, or `none` at the end

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Iteration.rux#L133)
